style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A wisdom psalm for everyone who will die, which is the audience it names: all peoples, low and high, rich and poor together. The sons of Korah promise a proverb and a riddle set to the lyre, and the riddle is this: why fear in evil days the men who trust their wealth? Because no man can ransom a brother -- the price of a soul is too high and must be let alone forever -- so the wise die like the fool and the brute, leave their estates to others, and name their lands after themselves while the grave becomes their real house. The refrain says it twice: man in his splendor does not last the night; he is like the beasts that perish. In between comes the most chilling line in the Psalter -- like sheep they are herded to Sheol, and Death is their shepherd -- and, against it, one of the Old Testament's clearest hopes beyond the grave: but God will ransom my soul from the grip of Sheol, for He will take me, the verb used of Enoch and Elijah. So do not be afraid when a man grows rich: he takes nothing down with him, and the applause stops at the family tomb. The last line changes one word in the refrain and solves the riddle: it is not splendor that makes a man a beast, it is splendor without understanding.

1.text: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. Hear this, all you peoples; give ear, all you who live in this passing world,
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] for ['of', ben, the KJV margin] the sons [ben] of Korah. Hear [shama] this, all you people [am -- peoples]; give ear [azan], all you inhabitants [yashab] of the world [cheled -- this fleeting age]:
1.notes: shimu-zot kol-ha-ammim (H8085, H5971): hear this, ALL peoples -- a wisdom psalm addressed, like Proverbs 8:4, to the whole race, not to Israel; haazinu kol-yoshebe chaled (H238, H3427, H2465): give ear, all who dwell in cheled -- the passing world, Psalm 17:14's word for the age that men of the world get their portion in. The audience is everyone who will die, which is the subject.

2.text: low-born and high-born together, rich and poor alike.
2.amp: Both low [ben adam -- sons of Adam] and high [ben ish -- sons of a man], rich [ashir] and poor [ebyon], together [yachad].
2.notes: gam-bene adam gam-bene ish (H1121, H120, H376): both sons of adam -- common humanity -- and sons of ish -- men of rank: the Hebrew's two words for man used as a class distinction (cf. Psalm 62:9); yachad ashir ve-ebyon (H3162, H6223, H34): together rich and poor. The one thing the rich and the poor do together is what the psalm is about.

3.text: My mouth will speak wisdom, and the murmuring of my heart will be understanding.
3.amp: My mouth [peh] shall speak [dabar] of wisdom [chokmot -- wisdoms]; and the meditation of my heart [leb] shall be of understanding [tebunah].
3.notes: pi yedabber chokhmot (H6310, H1696, H2454): my mouth will speak chokhmot -- the plural, Wisdom herself as in Proverbs 1:20; ve-hagut libbi tebunot (H3820, H8394): and the murmuring of my heart, understandings. The psalmist claims the sage's chair before he sits in it: verses 3-4 are the Psalter's fullest wisdom-preamble.

4.text: I will bend my ear to a proverb; I will open my riddle to the sound of the lyre.
4.amp: I will incline [natah] mine ear [ozen] to a parable [mashal -- proverb]: I will open [pathach] my dark saying [chidah -- riddle] upon the harp [kinnor -- lyre].
4.notes: atteh le-mashal ozni (H5186, H4912, H241): I will bend my ear to a mashal -- he listens before he teaches -- ephtach be-khinnor chidati (H6605, H3658, H2420): I will OPEN my riddle on the lyre -- chidah, Samson's word (Judges 14:12); a hard saying set to music so it will stay in the head. Psalm 78:2 uses the same pair, and Matthew 13:35 quotes it of Jesus' parables.

5.text: Why should I be afraid in evil days, when the guilt of those at my heels surrounds me --
5.amp: Wherefore should I fear [yare] in the days [yom] of evil [ra], when the iniquity [avon] of my heels shall compass [sabab] me about?
5.notes: lammah ira bi-yme ra (H3372, H3117, H7451): WHY should I fear in days of evil -- the riddle's question; avon aqebai yesubbeni (H5771, H5437): when the iniquity of my heels -- of those at my heels, my pursuers -- surrounds me. The 'heel' word is Jacob's (Genesis 25:26): the ones treading on him are the rich of verse 6.

6.text: men who rely on their wealth and brag about how much they own?
6.amp: They that trust [batach] in their wealth [chayil], and boast [halal] themselves in the multitude [rob] of their riches [osher];
6.notes: ha-botechim al-chelam (H982, H2428): those who TRUST in their chayil -- their strength, which for the rich means their money; u-be-rob oshram yithallalu (H7230, H6239, H1984): and in the abundance of their riches BOAST -- halal, praise aimed at a bank balance. Psalm 44:8's 'in God we boast' is the answer to this line.

7.text: No man can by any means ransom a brother, or give to God the price of his release --
7.amp: None of them can [ish] by any means redeem [padah -- ransom] his brother [ach], nor give [natan] to God [Elohim] a ransom [kopher -- covering price] for him:
7.notes: ach lo-phadoh yiphdeh ish (H251, H6299, H376): a brother -- 'ransoming, he cannot ransom', the doubled verb for emphasis -- no man can; lo-yitten l-Elohim kophro (H5414, H430, H3724): he cannot give God his kopher, the covering price, Exodus 30:12's ransom for a life. The riddle's answer begins: the one purchase money cannot make is the one that matters.

8.text: for the redemption of their soul is costly, and it must be let alone forever --
8.amp: (For the redemption of their soul [nephesh] is precious [yaqar -- costly], and it ceases [chadal -- must be left alone] for ever [olam]:)
8.notes: ve-yeqar pidyon naphsham (H3365, H5315): and COSTLY is the redemption of their soul -- yaqar, Psalm 116:15's precious -- ve-chadal le-olam (H2308, H5769): and it ceases forever -- one gives up on it entirely. The price is beyond any purse; only Mark 10:45's ransom ever met it, and it was not paid in silver (1 Peter 1:18-19).

9.text: that he should go on living forever and never see the pit.
9.amp: That he should still live [chayah] for ever [netsach], and not see [raah] corruption [shachat -- the pit].
9.notes: vi-chi-od la-netsach (H2421, H5331): that he should live on -- forever -- lo yireh ha-shachat (H7200, H7845): and not see the shachat, the pit, decay. Psalm 16:10's phrase, which Peter preached of the resurrection (Acts 2:27): the thing no rich man could buy for his brother, God did for His Son.

10.text: For he sees that even wise men die; the fool and the brute perish alike and leave their wealth to others.
10.amp: For he sees [raah] that wise men [chakam] die [muth], likewise [yachad] the fool [kesil] and the brutish person [baar] perish [abad], and leave [azab] their wealth [chayil] to others [acher].
10.notes: ki yireh chakhamim yamutu (H7200, H2450, H4191): for he SEES -- anyone can -- that the wise die; yachad kesil va-baar yobedu (H3162, H3684, H1198, H6): together the fool and the brute perish -- ve-azebu la-acherim chelam (H5800, H312, H2428): and leave their chayil to others. Ecclesiastes 2:16-18's complaint in one verse: wisdom does not exempt you, and the estate goes to someone else.

11.text: Their inner thought is that their houses will last forever, their dwellings for generation after generation; they name their lands after themselves.
11.amp: Their inward [qereb] thought is, that their houses [bayith] shall continue for ever [olam], and their dwelling [mishkan] places to all ['generation and generation', dor, the KJV margin] generations; they call [qara] their lands [adamah] after their own names [shem].
11.notes: qirbam battemo le-olam (H7130, H1004, H5769): their inside -- their unspoken assumption -- is that their houses are forever, mishkenotam le-dor va-dor (H4908, H1755): their dwellings for 'generation and generation', the margin's literal. qareu bi-shmotam ale adamot (H7121, H8034, H127): they have called lands by their own names -- the estate with the family name on the gate. The ancient Greek read 'their graves are their houses forever', which is what the psalm means.

12.text: But man in his splendor does not stay the night; he is like the beasts that are cut off.
12.amp: Nevertheless man [adam] being in honour [yeqar -- splendor] abides not [lun -- lodges, stays the night]: he is like [mashal] the beasts [behemah] that perish [damah -- are cut off, silenced].
12.notes: ve-adam bi-qar bal-yalin (H120, H3366, H3885): and man in splendor does not LODGE -- lun, to spend the night: he does not last till morning; nimshal ka-behemot nidmu (H4911, H929, H1820): he is likened to the beasts that are silenced. The refrain (v. 20 repeats it with one change): the rich man and his ox end the same way, and the ox never named a farm after itself.

13.text: This is the way of those who are foolishly confident, and of those after them who approve of their talk. Selah.
13.amp: This their way [derek] is their folly [kesel]: yet their posterity [achar -- those after them] approve ['delight in their mouth', ratsah, the KJV margin] their sayings [peh]. Selah [Selah].
13.notes: zeh darkam kesel lamo (H1870, H3689): this, their way -- kesel to them: folly, or the false confidence the word also means (Job 8:14); ve-acharehem be-phihem yirtsu (H310, H6310, H7521): and those after them 'delight in their mouth', the margin's literal -- the heirs quote the dead man's sayings admiringly and repeat his mistake. Selah, on a funeral eulogy.

14.text: Like sheep they are herded to Sheol; Death will be their shepherd; the upright will rule over them in the morning, and their form will be consumed by Sheol, far from any lofty dwelling.
14.amp: Like sheep [tson] they are laid in the grave [sheol]; death [mavet] shall feed [raah -- shepherd] on them; and the upright [yashar] shall have dominion [radah] over them in the morning [boqer]; and their beauty ['strength', tsur, the KJV margin] shall consume [balah -- wear away] in the grave [sheol] from their dwelling ['the grave being an habitation to every one of them', sheol, the KJV margin].
14.notes: ka-tson li-sheol shattu (H6629, H7585): like sheep they are SET for Sheol -- penned for it -- mavet yirem (H4194, H7462): Death will SHEPHERD them -- the psalm's most chilling line, the anti-Psalm 23: a shepherd who is the slaughterer. va-yirdu bam yesharim la-boqer (H7287, H3477, H1242): and the upright will rule over them in the MORNING -- the resurrection dawn of Psalm 17:15 and 30:5. ve-tsuram le-ballot sheol mi-zebul lo (H6697, H1086, H7585): and their form -- the margin's 'strength', tsur, the rock-word -- is for Sheol to wear away, far from the lofty house they built. The text is difficult; the picture is not.

15.text: But God will ransom my soul from the grip of Sheol, for He will take me. Selah.
15.amp: But God [Elohim] will redeem [padah -- ransom] my soul [nephesh] from the power ['hand', yad, the KJV margin] of the grave ['hell', sheol, the KJV margin]: for He shall receive [laqach -- take] me. Selah [Selah].
15.notes: akh-Elohim yiphdeh naphshi mi-yad-sheol (H430, H6299, H5315, H3027, H7585): BUT God will RANSOM my soul from the hand of Sheol -- padah, verse 7's verb, the ransom no man could pay, paid by God. ki yiqqacheni (H3947): for He will TAKE me -- laqach, the verb for Enoch (Genesis 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3), the two men death did not shepherd. The riddle's answer, and one of the Old Testament's clearest hopes beyond the grave; Selah, because it deserves the pause.

16.text: Do not be afraid when a man grows rich, when the glory of his house increases;
16.amp: Be not afraid [yare] when one [ish] is made rich [ashar], when the glory [kabod] of his house [bayith] is increased [rabah];
16.notes: al-tira ki-yaashir ish (H3372, H6238, H376): do not FEAR when a man gets rich -- verse 5's question answered as a command; ki-yirbeh kebod beto (H7235, H3519, H1004): when the kabod, the weight, of his house grows. Kabod is glory and it is also heaviness; the psalm will show which one the grave keeps.

17.text: for when he dies he will take nothing along; his glory will not go down after him.
17.amp: For when he dies [mavet] he shall carry nothing away [laqach -- take]: his glory [kabod] shall not descend [yarad] after [achar] him.
17.notes: ki lo be-moto yiqqach ha-kol (H4194, H3947): for at his death he will not TAKE the whole -- anything -- laqach, the verb God used of the psalmist in verse 15: God takes the man; the man takes nothing; lo-yered acharav kebodo (H3381, H310, H3519): his glory will not go down after him. Job 1:21 and 1 Timothy 6:7 say it plainly; the psalm says it with a pun.

18.text: Though while he lived he congratulated his soul -- and men praise you when you do well for yourself --
18.amp: Though while he lived ['in his life', chay, the KJV margin] he blessed [barak] his soul [nephesh]: and men will praise [yadah] you, when you do well [yatab] to yourself.
18.notes: ki-naphsho be-chayyav yebarekh (H5315, H2416, H1288): though his soul 'in his life' he blessed -- congratulated himself, the rich fool's 'soul, take thine ease' (Luke 12:19). ve-yodukha ki-tetib lakh (H3034, H3190): and men praise you when you do well for yourself -- the second person, suddenly, as if the psalmist were addressing the reader: yes, they will applaud. Then verse 19.

19.text: he will go to join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light again.
19.amp: He ['The soul shall', bo, the KJV margin] shall go [bo] to the generation [dor] of his fathers [ab]; they shall never [netsach] see [raah] light [or].
19.notes: tabo ad-dor abotav (H935, H1755, H1): 'the soul' -- the margin's subject -- will go to the generation of his fathers; ad-netsach lo yiru-or (H5331, H7200, H216): forever they do not see light. The applause of verse 18 ends at the family tomb, where it is dark; the psalmist has just said (v. 15) that God will take him somewhere else.

20.text: Man in his splendor, without understanding, is like the beasts that are cut off.
20.amp: Man [adam] that is in honour [yeqar -- splendor], and understands [bin] not, is like [mashal] the beasts [behemah] that perish [damah -- are cut off].
20.notes: adam bi-qar ve-lo yabin (H120, H3366, H995): man in splendor -- 'and does not UNDERSTAND': the refrain of verse 12 with one word changed, 'does not lodge' becomes 'does not understand'. That is the riddle solved: it is not splendor that makes a man a beast, it is splendor without insight. nimshal ka-behemot nidmu (H4911, H929, H1820): likened to the beasts that are silenced. The wise man of verse 3 has said his piece: two ways to die, and only one Shepherd worth having.
